To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new FCM cluster validity method, based on the redundancy between the clusters, improves both the quality of the FCM clustering and the computation time, when applied on IR spectral histology images of human skin cancer.

the proposed method is a new method for the estimation of FCM parameters that can improve the quality of the clustering and the computational time when applied to the spectral histology of skin tumors.

the redundancy of Fuzzy C-Mean clusters is a good criterion to choose the number of clusters in the FCM clustering algorithm and that this redundancy criterion is also well adapted for selecting the fuzziness parameter in the FCM algorithm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods to estimate the FCM parameters, in order to improve its performances and its applicability to the biomedical field.
the development of a new method for the selection of the FCM parameters and its application in biomedical IR hyperspectral image analysis.
a new method of parameter estimation for FCM clustering, which can be easily applied to any kind of hyperspectral data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new method is the most efficient one, and the best compromise between quality and computational time.

our new method is a very efficient tool for the estimation of the FCM parameters in the analysis of IR spectral histology of cancer, and should be used as a reference method for this purpose in the future.
, for the FCM parameter estimation, the proposed redundancy method outperforms the classical cluster validity indices, while being more robust than the m-rules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FCM parameter selection problem is a crucial step for a relevant analysis and interpretation of IR spectral histology of skin tumors.
we have proposed a new method based on a heuristic approach for selecting the number of FCM clusters and the fuzzification parameter.
the redundancy of FDM clusters is an efficient indicator for the selection of the number of FDM clusters, and that the m-rules can help for the determination of the FDM fuzziness parameter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given dataset, a single method cannot be considered as optimal for all values of the two parameters.
the redundancy of FMC clusters is a good indicator of the quality of a clustering, especially in biomedical applications.
the redundancy-based method is a powerful and fast tool to select the number of clusters in a biomedical application.
